########## scripts/run_e2e.sh ##########
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the hybrid e2e tests directly, bypassing the VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID
# CTest gate. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts in this
# workspace.
#
# Env overrides:
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64)
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under verilator/build/)
#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
#   MODE         marker | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 2 processes (qemu1, vsim); the
#                headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's own
#                scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)

set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
# vsim sim_* live in the external VSIM_BIN_DIR (setup.sh exports it, mirroring
# VSIM_QEMU); fall back to the legacy in-tree build only if it is unset.
VSIM_BUILD="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/verilator/build}"
HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"

VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  # Default to the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine (the same one ./andesim
  # pins). The fixtures are single-hart programs: on a multicore build like
  # sim_ax45mpv_mp2 -- which sorts FIRST under verilator/build/ -- the
  # secondary hart runs crt0 from reset, writes SKIPPED to SimControl and
  # stops the sim before hart 0 drains, failing every C fixture. Fall back
  # to the first sim_* only when the canonical engine is not built.
  VSIM_BIN="$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
  if [[ ! -x "$VSIM_BIN" ]]; then
    VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_BUILD"/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
  fi
fi

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

require() {
  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
    fail "$1 not found: $2"
    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
    exit 1
  fi
}
require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"

export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN

REQUIRED_ELFS=(
  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem
  rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode
  rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_fcsr rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs
  rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
  # CSR-less spin loop fixture.
  icount_spin
)
need_build=0
for f in "${REQUIRED_ELFS[@]}"; do
  [[ -e "$TEST_DIR/$f.elf" ]] || need_build=1
done
if (( need_build )); then
  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
fi

# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
RT_TESTS=(
  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip"
  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
  "rt_m_ext_counters|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_counters"
  "rt_m_ext_trigcause|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_trigcause"
  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_fcsr|FIXTURE=rt_c_fcsr"
  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_v_fill|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_fill"
  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
)

NEG_TESTS=(
  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
)

# Heavyweight round-trip fixtures, run SEQUENTIALLY after the parallel
# pool drains. The L6 privilege fixtures need an S/U-capable engine pair
# (the default ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only,
# NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1), and the only built RV64 one is
# ax66_makatau -- whose Verilator binary runs 32 threads. Two of those in
# the parallel pool saturate the box and time out BOTH themselves and the
# lighter default-engine tests, so they get the machine to themselves.
# Same entry format as RT_TESTS; both trigger modes still apply.
SERIAL_RT_TESTS=(
  "rt_priv_smode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_smode CHECK_PRIV=1 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
  "rt_priv_umode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_umode CHECK_PRIV=0 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
)

MODE="${MODE:-both}"
case "$MODE" in
  marker|pc|both) ;;
  *) fail "MODE must be one of marker|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
esac

default_jobs() {
  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
    fi
  fi
  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
  printf '%d\n' "$n"
}
JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }

FILTER="${FILTER:-}"

LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
: > "$LOCK_FILE"

# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
run_one() {
  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
  local start end elapsed status rc
  start=$(date +%s)
  set +e
  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  set -e
  end=$(date +%s)
  elapsed=$((end - start))
  case $rc in
    0)  status=PASS ;;
    77) status=SKIP ;;
    *)  status=FAIL ;;
  esac
  (
    flock 9
    case "$status" in
      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
    esac
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
}

# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
# matters: marker-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
declare -a WORKPLAN=()
for tm in marker pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    # B3: anchor the regex so FILTER=rt_csr does not silently also match
    # rt_csr_survival. Users who want a substring match pass '.*marker.*'.
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done
for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
done

# Serial phase: same (mode, name, cmd) tuples, executed one at a time
# after the parallel pool drains (see SERIAL_RT_TESTS above for why).
declare -a SERIAL_PLAN=()
for tm in marker pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${SERIAL_RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ ^$FILTER$ ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    SERIAL_PLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done

TOTAL=$(( ${#WORKPLAN[@]} + ${#SERIAL_PLAN[@]} ))
step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"

# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
  printf '.\n' >&8
done

i=0
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
  i=$((i+1))
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
  read -r -u 8 _tok
  (
    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
    printf '.\n' >&8
  ) &
done
wait
exec 8>&-

# Serial phase: each heavyweight test gets the machine to itself.
for w in "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
  i=$((i+1))
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
  run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
done

declare -A MODE_PASS=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_FAIL=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -A MODE_SKIP=([marker]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0)
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
  case "$r_status" in
    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
  esac
done < "$RESULTS_FILE"

# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
# deterministic post-run failure dump.
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}" "${SERIAL_PLAN[@]}"; do
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
    echo
    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
  fi
done

echo
marker_p=${MODE_PASS[marker]} marker_f=${MODE_FAIL[marker]} marker_s=${MODE_SKIP[marker]}
pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}

# Shared status printers for test scripts. Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# Repo root, derived from this lib's own location (tests/lib/ -> ../..).

# cfg_val KEY -> the value of KEY in the repo-root config.env ("" if absent).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ROI boundary resolution for pc-trigger mode.
#
# pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs: the ROI start (drain QEMU) and
# the ROI end (drain vsim). Either boundary may be named as a 0x-prefixed
# hex address (used verbatim) OR as a symbol present in the ELF (resolved
# against `nm --defined-only` output). This decouples the switch points from
# the workload source: any function can be the ROI, with no planted markers.

# resolve_pc <boundary> <nm_output>
#   <boundary>  : "0x<hex>" | "0X<hex>" | symbol name
#   <nm_output> : `nm --defined-only` listing ("addr type name" per line)
# Prints the bare hex address (no 0x) on stdout, or nothing if a symbol name
# is not found (the caller treats empty as a fatal "cannot resolve").
resolve_pc() {
  local boundary="$1" nm_out="$2"
  case "$boundary" in
    0x*|0X*) printf '%s\n' "${boundary#0[xX]}" ;;
    *)       printf '%s\n' "$nm_out" | awk -v s="$boundary" '$3==s{print $1; exit}' ;;
  esac
}

# roi_resolve_pair <nm_output> [<label>]
#   Reads ROI_START / ROI_END from the environment (both REQUIRED), resolves
#   each against <nm_output>, and sets the globals ENTER_PC / EXIT_PC (bare
#   hex). Returns 1 and prints a FAIL line naming the offending boundary if
#   either is unset or does not resolve. <label> tags the FAIL message.
roi_resolve_pair() {
  local nm_out="$1" label="${2:-pc}"
  local start="${ROI_START:-}"
  local end="${ROI_END:-}"
  if [ -z "$start" ] || [ -z "$end" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: ROI_START and ROI_END must both be set (0x address or symbol name)"
    return 1
  fi
  ENTER_PC=$(resolve_pc "$start" "$nm_out")
  EXIT_PC=$(resolve_pc "$end" "$nm_out")
  if [ -z "$ENTER_PC" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI start '$start' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$EXIT_PC" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI end '$end' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
    return 1
  fi
  return 0
}

# roi_markers_from_disasm <objdump_disasm>
#   Derives the two pc-mode switch PCs from the ROI marker HINTs a fixture
#   embeds, scanning `objdump -d` text:
#     ENTER = the entry marker     `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`  (encoding 5a002013)
#     EXIT  = the LAST exit marker `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1`  (encoding 5a102013)
#   Both are the marker PCs themselves: the plugin (enter_pc=) and vsim
#   (--hybrid-exit-pc) each resume one insn past the trigger
#   (compute_handoff_pc = vaddr+size), so feeding the marker PC reproduces
#   marker mode's switch points exactly -- no offset arithmetic here. EXIT
#   keeps the LAST marker so a fixture that jumps over poison exit-marker
#   padding (rt_pc_jump) resolves to the real, reachable exit, not the first
#   dead one. The raw-bytes match is mnemonic-independent, so no objdump
#   decode table is needed.
#   Prints "ENTER EXIT" as bare hex; returns 1 (prints nothing) if either
#   marker is absent. This lets the bulk runner drive pc mode with no
#   per-fixture config; ./andesim run still passes explicit boundaries.
roi_markers_from_disasm() {
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '
    $2 == "5a002013" && enter == "" { e = $1; sub(/:$/, "", e); enter = e }
    $2 == "5a102013"                { x = $1; sub(/:$/, "", x); exit_pc = x }
    END {
      if (enter != "" && exit_pc != "") { print enter, exit_pc }
      else                              { exit 1 }
    }
  '
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# RED->GREEN: resolve_pc maps an ROI boundary (a symbol name OR a 0x-hex
# address) to a bare hex address, resolving symbols against `nm` output.
# This is the primitive that lets pc mode point at ANY symbol/address
# instead of the planted _hybrid_enter_pc / _hybrid_exit_pc markers.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/roi.sh"

fail() { echo "FAIL[roi_resolve]: $1"; exit 1; }

# Fake `nm --defined-only` output (columns: addr type name).
NM_FIXTURE='0000000000100002 T _hybrid_enter_pc
0000000000100020 T _hybrid_exit_pc
0000000000100040 T vmatmul_kernel
0000000000100000 T main'

# 1. hex passthrough strips the 0x prefix, keeps the digits.
got=$(resolve_pc "0x100abc" "$NM_FIXTURE")
[ "$got" = "100abc" ] || fail "hex passthrough: want 100abc got '$got'"

# 2. uppercase 0X prefix also stripped.
got=$(resolve_pc "0X1f" "$NM_FIXTURE")
[ "$got" = "1f" ] || fail "0X prefix: want 1f got '$got'"

# 3. arbitrary symbol name resolves via nm output.
got=$(resolve_pc "vmatmul_kernel" "$NM_FIXTURE")
[ "$got" = "0000000000100040" ] || fail "symbol resolve: want ...100040 got '$got'"

# 4. unknown symbol -> empty (caller turns this into a FAIL).
got=$(resolve_pc "nope" "$NM_FIXTURE")
[ -z "$got" ] || fail "unknown symbol: want empty got '$got'"

# --- roi_resolve_pair: env-required + dual resolve, as e2e.sh uses it ---

# 5. unset ROI_START/ROI_END -> error (no implicit fallback).
unset ROI_START ROI_END
out=$(roi_resolve_pair "$NM_FIXTURE" t 2>&1)
[ $? -ne 0 ] || fail "unset pair: expected nonzero return"
case "$out" in *"ROI_START and ROI_END"*) ;; *) fail "unset pair: missing required-vars message: '$out'";; esac

# 6. ROI_START symbol + ROI_END hex resolve to ENTER_PC / EXIT_PC.
ROI_START=vmatmul_kernel ROI_END=0x100100 roi_resolve_pair "$NM_FIXTURE" t \
  || fail "override pair: returned nonzero"
[ "$ENTER_PC" = "0000000000100040" ] || fail "ENTER_PC: got '$ENTER_PC'"
[ "$EXIT_PC"  = "100100" ]            || fail "EXIT_PC: got '$EXIT_PC'"

# 7. an unresolvable boundary fails loudly and names the offender.
out=$(ROI_START=ghost ROI_END=main roi_resolve_pair "$NM_FIXTURE" myfix 2>&1)
[ $? -ne 0 ] || fail "bad start: expected nonzero return"
case "$out" in *"myfix"*"ghost"*) ;; *) fail "bad start: message missing label/symbol: '$out'";; esac

# --- roi_markers_from_disasm: derive pc-mode boundaries from ROI markers ----
# Lets the bulk runner drive pc mode with no per-fixture config: ENTER is the
# entry marker `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (enc 5a002013), EXIT is the LAST exit
# marker `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (enc 5a102013). Both are the marker PCs -- the
# plugin/vsim resume one insn past the trigger (compute_handoff_pc=vaddr+size),
# reproducing marker mode's switch points. Inputs are `objdump -d` fragments.

# 8. in-order fixture: entry marker -> single exit marker.
DISASM_INORDER='  10023c: 5a002013  slti zero,zero,1440
  100240: 5a102013  slti zero,zero,1441
  100244: 8082  ret'
got=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$DISASM_INORDER") \
  || fail "in-order: function returned nonzero"
[ "$got" = "10023c 100240" ] || fail "in-order: want '10023c 100240' got '$got'"

# 9. jump-over-poison fixture (rt_pc_jump): the c.j skips dead exit markers;
#    the LAST 5a102013 is the real, reachable exit -- not the first.
DISASM_JUMP='  100000: 5a002013  slti zero,zero,1440
  100004: a83d  c.j 0x100042
  100006: 5a102013  slti zero,zero,1441
  10000a: 5a102013  slti zero,zero,1441
  100042: 5a102013  slti zero,zero,1441
  100046: 4601  c.li a2,0'
got=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$DISASM_JUMP") \
  || fail "jump: function returned nonzero"
[ "$got" = "100000 100042" ] || fail "jump: want '100000 100042' (last exit) got '$got'"

# 10. no markers -> nonzero return, empty output.
DISASM_NONE='  100000: 1141  c.addi sp,sp,-16
  100002: 8082  ret'
got=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$DISASM_NONE"); rc=$?
[ "$rc" -ne 0 ] || fail "no-markers: expected nonzero return, got rc=0"
[ -z "$got" ]   || fail "no-markers: expected empty output, got '$got'"

echo "[roi_resolve] PASS"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# B2 lint: tests/e2e.sh must detach stdin (`</dev/null`) from every
# interactive-by-default subprocess it spawns (QEMU `-nographic`, vsim under
# `timeout`). Without it, a backgrounded shell group (scripts/run_e2e.sh uses
# one) lets SIGTTOU stop the child when it calls tcsetattr on the inherited
# controlling tty. Diagnostic tell: empty log + rc=124 + /proc/$PID/status
# State `T`. See memory `feedback_qemu_timeout_sigttou`.
#
# This is a static lint: it greps the QEMU1 and vsim invocation blocks in
# tests/e2e.sh for the `</dev/null` redirect. Catches accidental removal of
# the SIGTTOU workaround without needing a real QEMU/vsim build.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
E2E="$SCRIPT_DIR/e2e.sh"

fail() { echo "FAIL[e2e_stdin_detached]: $1"; exit 1; }

[ -r "$E2E" ] || fail "cannot read $E2E"

# Block 1: QEMU 1 spawn (no `timeout`, but `-nographic` + tty-inherited stdin
# is still SIGTTOU-prone under backgrounded shell groups).
qemu1_block=$(awk '/QEMU 1: drain entry state/,/^QEMU1_RC=/' "$E2E")
[ -n "$qemu1_block" ] || fail "QEMU 1 block not located"
echo "$qemu1_block" | grep -q '</dev/null' \
  || fail "QEMU 1 invocation missing </dev/null"

# Block 2: vsim spawn -- wrapped by `timeout`, which forks a new process
# group. tcsetattr on the inherited tty triggers SIGTTOU; the kernel stops
# the process and `timeout` eventually SIGKILLs at TIMEOUT.
vsim_block=$(awk '/vsim: resume \+ drain/,/^VSIM_RC=/' "$E2E")
[ -n "$vsim_block" ] || fail "vsim block not located"
echo "$vsim_block" | grep -q '</dev/null' \
  || fail "vsim invocation missing </dev/null"

echo "[e2e_stdin_detached] PASS"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# B3 lint: scripts/run_e2e.sh must anchor FILTER regex matches.
#
# The bash conditional `[[ "$name" =~ $FILTER ]]` does substring matching
# by default. With FILTER=rt_csr, the user expects a single fixture but
# rt_csr / rt_csr_survival both match (and any future rt_csr_*). To run
# multiple fixtures, the user can pass an explicit regex (e.g.
# FILTER='rt_csr.*'). The default policy is exact match.
#
# This static lint greps each FILTER comparison and requires the regex
# to be wrapped with `^` and `$`. Catches accidental removal of the
# anchors without needing a real test run.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
RUN_E2E="$SCRIPT_DIR/../scripts/run_e2e.sh"

fail() { echo "FAIL[run_e2e_filter_anchored]: $1"; exit 1; }

[ -r "$RUN_E2E" ] || fail "cannot read $RUN_E2E"

# Every `=~ ... $FILTER ...` should be of the form `=~ ^$FILTER$`.
matches=$(grep -nE '=~ +\^?\$FILTER\$?' "$RUN_E2E" || true)
[ -n "$matches" ] || fail "no FILTER regex sites found"

while IFS= read -r line; do
  if ! echo "$line" | grep -qE '=~ +\^\$FILTER\$'; then
    fail "unanchored FILTER regex at: $line"
  fi
done <<< "$matches"

echo "[run_e2e_filter_anchored] PASS"
